findings.subject: rules-app
findings.title: Service "rules-app" asks for linux/arm64 on a x86_64 host
findings.description: The manifest pins service "rules-app" to platform linux/arm64. This host is x86_64.
findings.why_it_matters: Without an emulation layer installed the container will not start at all. With one, it will start and run several times slower, which is harder to notice and worse to inherit.
findings.what_to_do: Remove the platform pin from "rules-app", or build an image for amd64.

findings.subject: ./missing.env
findings.title: env_file ./missing.env does not exist
findings.description: Service "rules-app" reads its environment from ./missing.env, and that file is not present next to the manifest.
findings.why_it_matters: Compose refuses to start a service whose env_file is missing. When it is present but empty the failure is worse — the service starts with none of its configuration and fails later, somewhere less obvious.
findings.what_to_do: Create ./missing.env before deploying, or remove the env_file entry from "rules-app".

evidence.output: no such file (the file's contents are never read by this audit)

findings.subject: 100.0 GiB
findings.title: The deployment asks for 100.0 GiB of memory; 18.4 GiB is available
findings.description: rules-app reserves 100.0 GiB. The host has 38.8 GiB total, 18.4 GiB available and 0 B of swap. This is computed from what the manifest declares, not from measured usage: actual consumption under load can be higher.
findings.why_it_matters: When memory runs out the kernel picks a process to kill, and its choice is not the one you would make. On a host with no swap the first symptom is usually an unrelated service disappearing.
findings.what_to_do: Lower the reservations, deploy fewer services on this host, or add memory. If the reservations are deliberately generous, this finding is the one to dismiss — after checking that they are.

findings.subject: rules-app
findings.title: Service "rules-app" is granted authority over the host
findings.description: Service "rules-app" declares: privileged: true, which disables essentially every container boundary; it bind-mounts the container runtime socket, which is equivalent to root on the host.
findings.why_it_matters: These flags are sometimes genuinely required — a monitoring agent, a backup tool, a container that manages other containers. The finding is not that they are wrong; it is that anyone who compromises this service has the host, and that has to be a decision somebody made on purpose rather than a line copied from an example.
findings.what_to_do: Confirm "rules-app" needs this. If it does, record why; if it does not, drop the flag — a specific cap_add is almost always enough where privileged was used.

evidence.output:
privileged: true, which disables essentially every container boundary
it bind-mounts the container runtime socket, which is equivalent to root on the host

findings.title: Subnet 10.250.73.0/24 overlaps an existing network
findings.description: Network "isolated" asks for 10.250.73.0/24, which overlaps 10.250.73.0/24 already used by the existing network "dwkit-net".
findings.why_it_matters: The engine refuses to create a network whose address range overlaps one it already has. When it does create it, routing between the two becomes ambiguous and the symptom appears later, as traffic reaching the wrong container.
findings.what_to_do: Choose a range outside 10.250.73.0/24 for "isolated", or reuse the existing network instead of declaring a new one.

findings.subject: /etc
findings.title: Bind mount of /etc exposes host state
findings.description: Service "rules-app" bind-mounts /etc into the container at /host-etc. That is host configuration.
findings.why_it_matters: A bind mount is not a copy. The container writes straight into the host path, and anything that goes wrong inside it goes wrong on the host.
findings.what_to_do: Mount a dedicated directory instead of /etc, or add `:ro` if the service only needs to read it.

findings.subject: /var/run/docker.sock
findings.title: Bind mount of /var/run/docker.sock exposes host state
findings.description: Service "rules-app" bind-mounts /var/run/docker.sock into the container at /var/run/docker.sock. That is the container runtime's own socket, which is equivalent to root on the host.
findings.why_it_matters: A bind mount is not a copy. The container writes straight into the host path, and anything that goes wrong inside it goes wrong on the host.
findings.what_to_do: Mount a dedicated directory instead of /var/run/docker.sock, or add `:ro` if the service only needs to read it.

findings.subject: nginx:latest
findings.title: Image nginx:latest is not pinned
findings.description: Service "rules-app" uses the `latest` tag, which is whatever the registry pushed most recently.
findings.why_it_matters: A tag can be moved. That makes the deployment unreproducible in the direction that matters: rolling back to "the version that worked" pulls whatever the tag points at today, and two hosts deployed a week apart from the same file are not running the same software.
findings.what_to_do: Pin nginx by digest (image@sha256:…) once you have the version you want.

findings.subject: rules-app
findings.title: 1 of 1 services define no healthcheck
findings.description: These services have no healthcheck: rules-app.
findings.why_it_matters: Without one, the engine reports a container as running the moment its process starts, which is not the same as the service being able to answer. A dependent service then starts against something that is not ready yet, and `depends_on` cannot help — it waits for "started", not for "working". A restart policy has the same blind spot: a process that is alive and wedged is never restarted.
findings.what_to_do: Add a healthcheck to the services other things depend on, at minimum.

findings.subject: 3 of 4
findings.title: There is no way back from this deployment
findings.description: The rollback plan for this host is incomplete. Missing: volume-backup: the deployment writes to bind /var/run/docker.sock (rules-app) and no backup location was found on this host, so a bad migration cannot be undone; proxy-config: apache configuration under /etc/httpd is not copied anywhere by this audit; take a copy before changing it, since a proxy that fails to start takes every site on this host down, not only the new one; snapshot: whether a hypervisor or provider snapshot of this host exists cannot be seen from inside it — confirm with whoever runs the infrastructure before deploying.
findings.why_it_matters: Every other finding in this report is about whether the deployment will work. This one is about what happens when it does not, and it is the only one that cannot be fixed after the fact.
findings.what_to_do: Before deploying: note the image digests currently running, copy the web server configuration somewhere outside this host, and take a snapshot or a volume backup.
